reasons: The cited clause p0072 expressly permits either Party (including Customer) to assign without consent to an affiliate, a purchaser of substantially all relevant assets, or a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, with all other assignments subject to consent not unreasonably withheld — this meets the preferred position on the Customer side and exceeds the mutual-notice fallback.
No change-of-control termination or re-pricing right in favour of the Vendor appears in the clause or elsewhere, so the walk-away scenarios are absent.

The two shortfalls noted (mutual rather than one-sided assignment freedom, and no express competitor-assignment bar) are minor sub-elements correctly noted in the rationale rather than flagged as deviations.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was applied and no comment was generated; the deterministic check confirms the successor/affiliate carve-out is present.
